If it is not possible to provide the actual sound at the time of filing, for example, when the applicant experiences difficulties in attaching a sound file to an electronically filed application, the medium incorporating the sound should be sent to the Office as soon as possible after the application is filed."},{"ref":"TMM/Part10/3/3/3/3","quote":"The representation of the trade mark may consist of a written description of sounds if the sign is not a musical-type sound."},{"ref":"TMM/Part10/3/3/3/3","quote":"A sign consisting of a musical sound might be most appropriately represented in the form of musical notation, however, this will depend on the trade mark."}],"answer":"## Fees to other bodies
The supplied passages do not establish whether an ordinary Australian trade mark application requires payments to bodies other than IP Australia, so I cannot give a general yes or no. They do identify an international-filing situation: under the Manual’s practice, an international application is filed with IP Australia through WIPO eFiling, but the international fees are paid directly to WIPO. [TMM/Part60/2/4/2/4/3~1]

## Representation, descriptions and extra material
- **Act requirement:** section 40 requires rejection if the trade mark cannot be represented graphically. **Manual practice:** the Registrar requires a graphical representation in the application. These are distinct: the Act states the rejection ground; the Manual states the filing practice. [TMA1995/s40; TMM/Part10/3/3/1]
- **All non-traditional marks — Manual practice:** a mark consisting of or containing a colour, scent, shape, sound, aspect of packaging or other non-traditional sign must also have a concise and accurate description. The description is entered as an endorsement and, together with the graphical representation, helps define the registration’s scope. [TMM/Part10/3/3/1]
- **Sound marks — Manual practice:** in most cases, provide a copy of the actual sound on a medium allowing easy copying, storage and replay, such as a CD, DVD or digital sound file. If you cannot supply it when filing, send it as soon as possible afterwards. A non-musical sound may be represented graphically by a written description; musical notation may be appropriate for a musical sound, depending on the mark. [TMM/Part10/3/3/3/4; TMM/Part10/3/3/3/3]
- **Three-dimensional shape marks — Manual practice:** an actual sample may also be required; the passage does not make this universal. [TMM/Part10/3/3/1]

The supplied passages do not specify additional file formats or samples for other non-traditional marks beyond the general representation and description requirements."}
